This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-realtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-realtime/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/realtime_subscription.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via data.record.updated (literal, a string literal in RealtimeEventType; a string literal in replacement; a string literal in semantic), data.records.updated (literal, a string literal in RealtimeEventType; a string literal in a comment in RealtimeEventPayload; a string literal in replacement; a string literal in semantic))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-realtime/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/realtime_subscription.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f11b5f20a2ee22698c6647c2fb76aa67e99a7a53` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5187981860e61c1a229a97589428eaba236d25e4` — the merge of head `17612ad5eaf0c3cac6e67f6a03daf04eb952051e` into base `f11b5f20a2ee22698c6647c2fb76aa67e99a7a53`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5187981860e61c1a229a97589428eaba236d25e4 && git checkout 5187981860e61c1a229a97589428eaba236d25e4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f11b5f20a2ee22698c6647c2fb76aa67e99a7a53 17612ad5eaf0c3cac6e67f6a03daf04eb952051e && git checkout -B drift-repro f11b5f20a2ee22698c6647c2fb76aa67e99a7a53 && git merge --no-ff 17612ad5eaf0c3cac6e67f6a03daf04eb952051e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f11b5f20a2ee22698c6647c2fb76aa67e99a7a53
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f11b5f20a2ee22698c6647c2fb76aa67e99a7a53` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `0b2a76726c6503d31ca13962d7260c2fe0438ac9`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20288 (body + 5 comments: first grade `5859582726`, retriage request `5881693927`, re-grade `5882152948`, claim `5882309567`, dev report `5883321020`); rulings by id — #14646 A (`5542632689`), #8347 甲 (`5791499872`), #14446 direction (`5506262367`); PR #20567 body, file list (11 files, +399 −55, matches `git diff origin/main...0b2a767` byte-for-byte on the stat) and the net diff against merge-base `ba5927f714`; the 39 check-runs on the head. All seven required contexts `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`). Every other run `success` or `skipped` (path-filtered `Console Pin Gate`, opt-in tarball smoke, the second-trigger duplicates of `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size`). No path is a governed surface; head repo = base repo; 454 changed lines. PR is draft, unarmed, unqueued — correct for a `needs:contract-review` head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`RealtimeEventType` accept set** (`@objectstack/spec/api`, a real `exports` entry): FROM {`record.created`, `record.updated`, `record.deleted`, `field.changed`} TO {`data.record.created`, `data.record.updated`, `data.record.deleted`, `data.records.updated`, `data.records.deleted`} — exactly `DataEventType` ∪ `BulkDataEventType` (`events.zod.ts:138-142`, `:172-175`), pinned equal to that union in `realtime.test.ts`. Widens by five, narrows by four. **Right.**
2. **Doors that parse it:** `SubscriptionEventSchema.type` (`realtime.zod.ts:115`, the only schema reader) and therefore `SubscriptionSchema.events[]` and `RealtimeConfigSchema.subscriptions[].events[]` (`.passthrough()` on other keys, strict on this enum). All three now refuse each retired value with its own prescription (`invalid_value` at `['events', 0, 'type']`, pinned through `SubscriptionSchema`); the error map returns `undefined` for any other input so a typo keeps zod's own message — the `HookBodyCapability` / `RuntimeMode` precedent, verified same shape (`hook-body.zod.ts`, `kernel/context.zod.ts`). No other spec schema embeds these doors (repo grep: comments and the migration entry only); `stack.zod.ts` has no realtime key; nothing outside `packages/spec` imports them. **Right, and the changeset names exactly these three doors.**
3. **Doors whose accept set does NOT move, correctly left:** `protocol.zod.ts#RealtimeSubscribeRequestSchema.events` is `z.array(z.string())`; `websocket.zod.ts#EventSubscriptionSchema.events` is `EventPatternSchema`; `contracts/realtime-service.ts#RealtimeSubscriptionOptions.eventTypes` is `string[]`; `RealtimeEventPayload.type` / `RealtimeEventSchema.type` are `string`. Only their example prose moved, where it was stale. **Right.**
4. **TS narrowing:** `RealtimeEventType`, `SubscriptionEvent`, `Subscription`, `RealtimeConfig` are `z.input` of the enum, so `tsc` refuses the old literals — stated in the changeset. **Right.**
5. **Producers untouched — the card's ⛔ holds.** `objectql/src/engine.ts` `publishDataEvent` (`:7099-7118`, `data.record.${action}`, parsed through `DataEventSchema`, envelope `payload: { ...event }`), `publishBulkDataEvent` (`:7198-7215`, `data.records.${action}`), `metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts` (`:695-723`, `metadata.${type}.${action}` gated by `MetadataEventType`, 39 members). None is in the file list. The runtime's published names do not change. **Right** (#14446 direction: repoint the enum, never the runtime).
6. **No transport, no route, no client subscribe primitive.** The 11 paths touch no `packages/rest`, `packages/runtime`, `packages/client`, no route table, no ws/sse dependency; the `in-memory-realtime-adapter.ts` change is a docblock `@example` only. #14646 ruling A and #8347 ruling 甲 hold. **Right.**
7. **`metadata.*` deliberately not members.** A `SubscriptionEvent` is record-shaped (`object` names a data object, `filters` narrows records); metadata events have their own closed `MetadataEventType` and their own client primitive `subscribeMetadata` (`client/src/realtime-api.ts:73`); adding 39 names would widen past the re-grade. The new `RealtimeEventPayload.type` example `'metadata.object.updated'` is a real member (`events.zod.ts:19`) on a `string` field the envelope genuinely carries. **Right.**
8. **Every prescription is true of the code:** each retired value names an emitted twin that exists; "`data.records.*` carries a count and no record" — `BulkDataEventSchema` has no `recordId`; "`field.changed` → `data.record.updated`, read the field from `changes`" — `DataEventSchema.changes` exists; "no event is published per field" — no producer does. **True.**
9. **The version each prescription names — `@objectstack/spec 17.5.0`:** spec is `17.4.0` on `origin/main`; pending changesets include many `minor` and no `major`, and `check-changeset-no-major` refuses a `major` (launch-window guard) — so the release that carries this is 17.5.0. ADR-0087's amended level ruling says a tombstone names the npm release it ships in, never the protocol major; the same `17.5.0` form is already on 21 sites in 14 files at `main`. **True of the release that will carry it** (see ③ for the one caveat shared with those 21 sites).
10. **Regenerated reference `content/docs/references/api/realtime.mdx`:** description equals the new `.describe()`, Allowed Values are the five, the `Subscription` / `SubscriptionEvent` tables show the new enum, `RealtimeEvent.type` example moved; produced by the repo's generator (`check:docs` inside the green `TypeScript Type Check`). **True.**
11. **README / adapter `@example`:** the published object `{ id: uuid, type, object, recordId, after, timestamp }` is a valid `DataEvent` (required: `id`, `type`, `object`, `recordId`, `timestamp`) and is what `engine.ts` wraps as `payload`; `subscribe('records', cb, { object, eventTypes })` matches `RealtimeSubscriptionOptions`; "the engine publishes `data.record.created` / `data.record.updated` with the full record body (`after`)" matches `engine.ts`. **True.**
12. **Enum docblock:** "Nothing in the open framework parses a subscription" — true (ledger census, no importer outside spec); "`realtime.test.ts` pins this enum equal to their union" — true; the old `NOT YET ENFORCED` block is replaced by a sentence that stays true (the vocabulary now fires; the container is still unparsed, and the docblock says so). **True.**
13. **D3 entry text:** "`field.changed` … DataEventType already dropped in protocol 17 (`data-field-changed-event-retired`)" — that entry sits in `step17` (`registry.ts:2138`, `toMajor: 17`); "`stack.zod.ts` has no realtime key" — 0 hits; "maintainer ruling of 2026-09-04: realtime stays out of open core" — #14646 A. `surface` / `replacement` carry no backticks or pipes as `build-upgrade-guide.ts` needs. `entries/semantic/18.*.ts` and the `registry.ts` copy are the house pattern (`check:migration-registry` green). **True.**
14. **Ledger:** one-line `_note` addition only; all six rows stay `dead` (they land `live-elsewhere` only when a channel-serving occupant parses the contract — re-grade `5882152948`); `Spec property liveness` green; no `state-counts.md` change owed. **Right.**
15. **PR body:** every sentence checked against the diff — "Closes #20288" (the card's claim names this branch; check green), the enum description, the five bullets, "No transport, no route and no client subscribe primitive", the session-URL footer. **All true.** `RealtimeEventPayload.type` and `RealtimeEvent.type` examples are both in the diff as stated.
16. **objectui at the pin `dd3f7e1b`:** 0 hits for `RealtimeEventType` or any old spelling (grep at the pinned commit) — the Console Pin Gate is unaffected, as the dev measured.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/spec`: `minor`** with the `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM → TO mapping, the one-line fix, and the marker `adr-0087: registered realtime-event-type-unemitted-values-retired` (an HTML-comment marker in the changeset; the gate resolved it — `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` green). Matches ADR-0087's amended level ruling (pre-GA, a metadata-facing retirement ships `minor`; the banner and the disposition carry breaking-ness) and AGENTS.md (`yes` ⇒ at least `minor`; `(narrowing)` ⇒ BREAKING). **Right.**
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`** in the PR body and the changeset. **Right.** The criterion is "does this widen the accept set or the public surface" — five values now parse that were refused before, so `yes`; four are refused that parsed before, so `(narrowing)`. This is the exact shape the gate's own fixture names ("a diff that widens AND narrows"). The pure-removal precedents that declared `no` (`17707`, `19116`, `20295`) removed without adding and are not this case.
- **ADR-0087 disposition: D3 semantic entry, no D2 conversion — fits.** ADR-0087 D2 does list "enum re-spellings" as lossless, but D2 is applied by the loader to metadata sources, and a `Subscription` is reachable from no such seam: not a stack collection member (`stack.zod.ts` has no realtime key), not a metadata type, not embedded in any other spec schema, not imported outside spec. A conversion entry would be a declared transform nothing ever runs — the declared≠enforced shape ADR-0049 forbids. Established: 47 `step18` semantic entries are D3-only for the same reason (error codes, contract-map entries, REST config keys, route params). `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` correctly untouched — an enum value is not a key. The `(narrowing)` arm and a D3-without-D2 entry are consistent: the prescription lives on the enum's error map, which IS the door.
- **`@objectstack/service-realtime`: `patch`.** README ships in the tarball (`files`), the `@example` ships in `dist` `.d.ts`; a stale example that could never fire is a documentation defect in a released package (precedent `17152`). `skip-changeset` would have been wrong. **Right.**

- **`service-knowledge` `record.*` branch left unmoved** (`knowledge-service-plugin.ts:218-231`, TSDoc `:24`, `knowledge-service.ts:232`, `:252`) — reads `event.type` as a plain `string` off its own `IRealtimeService` subscription, never the enum or `SubscriptionSchema`; dead before and after; leaving it in this PR is **right**. But it is a consumer-side legacy-shape fallback (`payload.record ?? payload`, Prime Directive #12 class) plus stale TSDoc, and "承接者:无" is not a carrier — under Prime Directive #10 the reviewer files a note that is a contract violation. **Escalated: the seat files a `domain:services` card** (dedupe words: knowledge-event-sync, record.created legacy branch, handleRecordUpsert payload.record).

The dev stayed inside the claim's surface and reported it, so nothing is buried — but leaving it leaves one shipped sentence false. **Escalated with a carrier:** a one-clause qualifier mirroring the JSON `_note` ("repointed by #20288; member list as measured at 5f5511f0"), either folded into this PR before enqueue or a docs-only follow-up the seat files; `check-liveness.mts:452-458` (same sentence; `scripts/` is outside `files`, so not shipped) rides that same fix. Not a blocker: the accept set, the prescriptions, the reference page and the changeset are all true.
- **`websocket.zod.ts:104` describe example `"record.*"`** — an `EventPatternSchema` wildcard on spelling (2), an open door whose accept set did not move; correctly fenced to the five-spelling convergence stage the re-grade reserved. *Answered: stays with that stage's card.*

- **Version caveat, shared with 21 existing sites:** "17.5.0" is true only while 17.5.0 is uncut. If the maintainer cuts 17.5.0 before this lands, this PR's four prescriptions go stale together with every pending tombstone at `main` — a fleet convention, not this PR's defect; the seat re-dates before enqueue if that happens.
